comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C1, C2, C16 regarding scale invariance. Both evaluations find the experimental demonstration of eigenspectrum collapse convincing and well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes robustness across datasets while peer reviewers highlight it as a surprising and key strength.

Strong agreement on claims C3, C4, C24, C26 regarding the ERM model. Both evaluations recognize the model as an important advance that successfully reproduces experimental features. Peer reviewers explicitly call it 'analytically tractable' and matching 'nontrivial features,' aligning with OpenEval's assessment of theoretical validation.

Agreement on claims C17-C21 regarding ruling out alternative models. Both evaluations accept that conventional models fail to capture scale invariance. OpenEval provides more detailed assessment of each alternative, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these control analyses without challenge.

Partial overlap on experimental methodology. OpenEval R4 focuses specifically on claim C13 (saturation behavior), while peer R4 addresses broader methodology (C9, C10, C13). Both find the experimental approach sound, though peer reviewers provide less detailed assessment of the saturation finding.

Disagreement on claim C32 regarding collapse index comparisons. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with quantitative evidence across datasets, while peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, requesting more rigorous quantitative validation of CI comparisons between null models and data.

Agreement on claims C35, C36 regarding robustness to spatial distributions and geometries. Both evaluations accept these simulation-based robustness checks. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the systematic testing, while peer reviewers implicitly accept through general endorsement of the model's tractability.

Agreement on claims C44-C48 regarding behavior-independent scale invariance and functional reorganization during hunting. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval emphasizes the anatomical consistency, while peer reviewers accept the subsampling analyses without raising concerns.

Agreement on experimental methodology claims C9, C10. Both evaluations accept the imaging methods and ROI analysis as sound. OpenEval provides specific methodological details while peer reviewers offer general acceptance of the experimental approach without critique.

Disagreement on speculative claims C49, C50, C58. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting these are speculative interpretations without direct validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED, accepting them as legitimate discussion points. Note peer R8 also includes C56 which OpenEval addresses separately in R10.

Partial overlap on claim C56 regarding finite dimensionality implications. OpenEval R10 rates C53 and C56 as SUPPORTED based on theoretical analysis and experimental data. Peer R8 groups C56 with speculative interpretations (C49, C50, C58) and accepts them as discussion points without distinguishing the theoretical basis.

OpenEval evaluated claims C5, C6, C7, C51 regarding established background knowledge and found them well-supported by literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not assess background/contextual claims.
